description: Somos QOYLLUR, un equipo participante del NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, con el lema “Ideas que iluminan”. Desarrollamos una aplicación web para monitorizar la salud de los astronautas mediante datos, gráficos de tendencias y alertas informativas. Nos motiva la innovación espacial y el trabajo colaborativo. Nos interesan la programación, el desarrollo web, la inteligencia artificial y el análisis de datos.
summary:
On long space missions, isolation, confinement and distance from Earth can turn a health problem into a critical one far from immediate medical care. That is why we built KAUSAY, a bilingual (Spanish/English) web platform that brings physical tracking, emotional wellbeing and crew collaboration into one place, so astronauts can assess their own health and act early.

Users can log vital signs, symptoms and authorized medical history, keep a private record, follow their evolution in a personal dashboard, and run standard or emergency evaluations, even for a crewmate. Using AI (Gemini) and public NASA resources, KAUSAY combines the available data to offer contextual preliminary guidance, warnings and follow-up recommendations, without replacing medical staff or issuing definitive diagnoses. It flags incomplete information and triggers the emergency protocol before consulting Gemini. Órbita, our conversational assistant, supports astronauts through isolation, stress, living together and distance from Earth, drawing on research and astronaut accounts.

KAUSAY includes invitation-based teams, differentiated permissions, encryption of sensitive data and user-controlled clinical memory. It matters because it brings scattered information together and supports better-informed human decisions where time, resources and communication are limited. Caring for health also means sustaining the mission.
details:
We developed Kausay, a web platform with space crews that brings together physical health, emotional wellbeing and possible diagnoses of your health. The system distinguishes routine checkups, with mandatory information, from emergencies or symptoms in order to start the process (wellbeing). In critical situations it shows immediate instructions on how to find professional help.

Through the Gemini API and retrieval of official NASA references, analyzing only authorized information, it generates contextualized guidance and warnings, without replacing a professional diagnosis. Órbita, our wellbeing assistant, offers conversational support in the face of isolation, stress and living together. Teams work through invitations and differentiated permissions.

We use HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the interface; Node.js, Express and EJS for the application; MongoDB with Mongoose for persistence; and the Gemini API for artificial intelligence. We incorporate AES-256-GCM encryption, consent, access controls and automated tests. Logging is manual: we do not integrate physical sensors.

Our innovation consists of integrating preventive care, emergency response and emotional support into one secure experience. We aspire to improve monitoring and support human decisions during prolonged missions and limited communications.
